passage:
Come, sit, Vaibhav. It's Yamini Aunty. I saw you on the terrace yesterday, just staring. Since your Dada died you've barely said a word, haven't you?
Let me tell you about my Nani. I was fifteen when she went, and for two days I felt nothing at all. I poured tea for the guests like a machine. Then, in maths class, the smell of a pencil box made me sob so hard I had to leave.
It comes in waves, beta, and never on time. My aunts made me sit with them at the prayers and tell stories about her. I laughed once, then cried harder, and both were allowed.
You needn't hurry any of it. Tell me one thing about your Dada. Just one.

qa.q: What made Yamini sob in maths class?
qa.a: The smell of a pencil box made her sob so hard she had to leave.

qa.q: What did Yamini feel during the first two days after her Nani died?
qa.a: She felt nothing at all: she was numb and poured tea for the guests like a machine.

qa.q: What could Vaibhav do while coping with the loss of his Dada?
qa.a: He can talk about his Dada, join the family prayers and let himself feel whatever comes, without hurrying.

qa.q: How might Yamini's aunts have felt making her sit with them at the prayers?
qa.a: They probably wanted to keep her close in the family's grief and help her remember her Nani, so her laughing and crying showed them she was letting it out.

grounding: An elder recalls her own numbness and sudden weeping after a grandparent's death, showing grief in waves, rituals and talking about the loved one.

passage:
Thursday. Biji's bhog was today at the gurdwara. Everyone cried during the ardas except me. I just stood there looking at the ceiling fan, feeling nothing, and I thought something must be wrong with me. Then tonight I opened the cupboard for a blanket and found her reading glasses in the pocket of her grey shawl. I sat on the floor and cried so hard I couldn't breathe properly. Mum came in and just held me. She said grief is like the sea at Juhu: it goes out and then comes back without asking. I told her I felt bad about not crying earlier. She said numb is also grief. Arnab messaged later, 'Want to talk about her?' I told him about Biji's terrible jokes and her rajma. It helped to say her name. Tomorrow I'll help Mum sort her things. Slowly.
- Amandeep

qa.q: What did Amandeep find in the pocket of Biji's grey shawl?
What was Amandeep feeling during the ardas?
qa.a: Amandeep felt numb, then worried that something was wrong for not crying like everyone else.

qa.q: What helped Amandeep let the grief move?
qa.a: Talking about Biji's jokes and rajma with Arnab, being held by Mum, and joining the rituals slowly without rushing.

qa.q: How does Mum see Amandeep's numbness at the bhog?
qa.a: She sees it as part of grief too, like a wave that goes out and comes back 🤍

grounding: A diary showing a teen numb at a grandparent's rituals, then suddenly weeping, learning that grief comes in waves and talking about her.

passage:
Payal: you ok? you were so quiet in class
Tarun: weirdly fine. that's the problem
Tarun: thatha died on monday and I've felt nothing. I even laughed at a meme today. who does that
Payal: grief is weird. my mum says it comes in waves
Tarun: then the wave came at the bus stop
Tarun: some uncle's phone was playing that old carnatic song thatha hummed every morning. I just started crying in front of everyone
Payal: oh tarun
Payal: do you want to tell me about him? only if you want
Tarun: he used to wake me at 5 for the milk queue and pretend it was an adventure
Tarun: his 13th day ceremony is on sunday. I was going to skip, say I have tuition
Payal: maybe go? you don't have to be ok there
Tarun: yeah. amma asked me to read the verse he liked. I think I will
Payal: call me after, whatever time

qa.q: What did Thatha use to do at five in the morning?
qa.a: He woke Tarun for the milk queue and pretended it was an adventure.

qa.q: Why was Tarun worried about feeling fine?
qa.a: Tarun felt numb and a bit guilty, thinking laughing at a meme meant something was wrong.

qa.q: What would you advise Tarun about the thirteenth-day ceremony?
qa.a: Go and read the verse Thatha liked, without needing to be okay, since the ritual can help carry the grief.

qa.q: How does Payal see Tarun's sudden crying?
qa.a: Payal sees it as a normal wave of grief and responds gently, inviting Tarun to share memories.

grounding: A chat showing a teen numb after a grandfather's death who suddenly weeps, and chooses to talk about him and join the family ritual.
